svg.title: RNA processing and quality control
svg.desc: The m7G cap is linked five-prime to five-prime through three phosphates. Splicing uses a branch-point two-prime hydroxyl followed by the upstream exon three-prime hydroxyl. In the common mammalian NMD rule, a premature stop is more than fifty to fifty-five nucleotides upstream of the final exon junction; the EJC itself sits about twenty to twenty-four nucleotides upstream of that junction.
svg.text: 1 A cap is an unusual connection
The cap supports stability and cap-dependent translation.
A poly-A tail is added separately at the 3′ end, without a DNA template.
2 Splicing uses two different hydroxyl groups
First: branch-point A 2′-OH attacks the 5′ splice site.
Then: upstream exon 3′-OH attacks the 3′ splice site.
Result: joined exons + a released lariat intron.
ATP powers rearrangements, not the two bond-exchange reactions.
3 Measure NMD distance to the junction
A downstream EJC can support decay after premature termination.
Common mammalian rule; exceptions exist. Schematic, not to scale.
